neighbours.label: an opening straight double quote that splices a quoted fragment into a running sentence after a comma ('the damage was severe, "far beyond anything' 0.39); sentence-initial quotes, closing quotes, parentheses, single quotes and curly quotes in the same sentences are quiet (0.02-0.03)
fire: The inspector wrote that the roof was unsafe, "liable to collapse under the first heavy snow."
Her lawyer insisted the contract was void, "signed under duress and never witnessed."
The committee found the spending justified, "within the limits set by the original grant."
He described the river crossing as routine, "something the ferrymen did twice a day."
The farmer called the harvest disappointing, "the worst since the floods of 1987."
The doctor rated the fracture as minor, "likely to heal in six weeks without surgery."
The reviewer judged the film overlong, "padded with scenes that go nowhere."
The surveyor called the boundary unclear, "marked only by a line of old hawthorns."
quiet: "The roof is liable to collapse under the first heavy snow," the inspector wrote.
Her lawyer insisted the contract was void because it was signed under duress and never witnessed.
The committee found the spending justified and within the limits of the original grant.
He described the river crossing as routine (the ferrymen did it twice a day).
The farmer called the harvest 'disappointing' and the worst since the floods of 1987.
The doctor said the fracture was minor; it should heal in six weeks without surgery.
"Padded with scenes that go nowhere," was how the reviewer described the film.
The surveyor called the boundary unclear, marked only by a line of old hawthorns on the map.
